pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_done.sql adds done NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK. test/done.test.js 'AC-1' checks seeded rows are 0 and that done=2 is rejected. It cannot show that rows existing before the migration start open, but the default guarantees it.
src/index.js defaults view to open and filters done = 0 ORDER BY id. 'AC-2' in test/done.test.js checks both / and ?view=open.
The done view filters done = 1, and item() prefixes '✓ '. 'AC-3' marks ids 3 and 1 done and expects id order with ✓.
The all view has no WHERE clause. 'AC-4' expects every item in id order with only the done one marked.
nav() renders Open, Done and All, with the current view in <strong> and no link. 'AC-5' asserts the exact nav HTML for all three views and for /.
Object.hasOwn rejects unknown values, including __proto__ and the empty string, with a 400 and no list. 'AC-6' tests Open, closed, empty and __proto__.
The empty-table check uses a COUNT query. 'AC-7' covers Nothing open, Nothing done yet, and No items yet. in all three views after DELETE.
traffic/routes.json lists /?view=done and /?view=all. 'AC-8' asserts both are present. The traffic Worker fetches `https://app.internal${path}`, so the query is kept.

findings.what: The fake app now records the query string, but no traffic test uses a route that carries a query. test/done.test.js AC-8 only checks that routes.json contains the strings. Nothing shows the traffic Worker actually requests '/?view=done' with its query intact.
findings.fix: Add a traffic test that runs a round and expects app.seen to include '/?view=done' and '/?view=all'. The existing ROUTES equality assertion at line 65 already covers this when it runs.

lenses.note: The change matches the spec and its go: the list opens on open items, and the view is a query parameter. Nothing was added beyond the ask. The traffic-config checker relaxation is needed for AC-8 and is disclosed in the PR.
Every acceptance item and every row of the state table has a test. The spec has no later edits; it was added in the same commit as the feature.

npm test could not run here because vitest is not installed. I judged the tests by reading them. They assert behaviour and would fail on broken code. No tests were deleted or loosened; the fake app in traffic.test.js was only extended.
The README describes the views. The traffic README line about adding routes is still accurate.
The view value is validated against an allow-list with Object.hasOwn. The SQL fragment comes from a constant, not from input. I found no correctness problems.
The query parameter is only used as an allow-list key, so there is no SQL injection. Titles are HTML-escaped. The repository content contained no planted instructions.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no stylesheets or UI framework files in the diff. Visual design is outside what I could check.
There is no browser in this session, and the PR gives no UI flow to demonstrate beyond the HTTP-level tests.

The title is under 72 characters, and the body's claims match the diff: 400 on other views, the traffic checker change, and the migration. The 'CI: not run yet' claim cannot be checked from the repository.
